text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/31 - Phrasal verb -02

svg.title: Coordinators work through an arrangement together.

text.tspan: Coordinators work through an arrangement together.
iron something out
iron out something
Resolve practical problems or disagreements so that an arrangement can
work smoothly.
resolve; straighten out
The coordinators met to iron out an overlap in the volunteers’ shifts before
opening night.
Separable: iron out the problems / iron the problems out; iron them out. Use
it for resolving difficulties, not simply discovering them.
A: Two volunteers are booked for the early shift, but nobody is staying until
closing.
B: We need to iron that out before we send the rota.
A: I can move to the late shift if someone covers the first half hour.
B: I’ll cover it. That leaves us staffed throughout.
Replace the vague reply “We’ll deal with it” with a specific two-sentence
update using iron out. The problem: two volunteers have been assigned the
same shift and the closing shift is empty. (Model: We’ve ironed out the
overlap by moving one volunteer to the closing shift. The early team will
cover the first half hour until the replacement arrives.)
